proposals.title: Scheduled Fading of GenAI Feedback
proposals.full_title: Scheduled Fading of GenAI Feedback: Effects on Evaluative Judgement and AI-Unassisted Scientific Argumentation
proposals.setting: University of Surrey, United Kingdom · proposed host institution
proposals.summary: A submitted international postdoctoral-research fellowship proposal on gradually reducing GenAI feedback and supporting learners’ independent evaluative judgement and scientific argumentation.
proposals.scope: The proposed work connects feedback design with learners’ capacity to judge evidence and construct arguments without AI assistance. Planned academic activities include refining the conceptual framework and protocol, piloting the feedback-fading design and measures, analysis, interpretation and scholarly outputs.
proposals.relationship: Prof. Naomi Winstone is the proposed overseas academic host. The formal host invitation supports the application; the visit has not begun and depends on the funding decision and relevant institutional arrangements.
proposals.limits: A host invitation and a submitted application are not a fellowship award. The proposed visit dates are not a confirmed funded appointment.

proposals.title: SciEpi-Feedback
proposals.full_title: Human–AI Feedback for Scientific Reasoning and Epistemic Agency
proposals.summary: A proposed international network linking human–AI feedback, scientific reasoning and epistemic agency across educational research contexts.
proposals.scope: The proposal aims to connect researchers around shared conceptual frameworks, assessment protocols and professional-learning resources. Its networking focus is distinct from the funding of an already running experimental research project.
proposals.relationship: Submission to COST Open Call OC-2026-1 was confirmed on 27 October 2026. A network-of-proposers record is not an awarded COST Action or a confirmed funded appointment for individual collaborators.
proposals.limits: No COST funding award, Action start date or appointed working-group leadership is announced here.

proposals.title: RECLAIM
proposals.full_title: When Delegation Changes the Capacity to Judge
proposals.setting: Kırşehir Ahi Evran University · proposed host institution
proposals.summary: A research proposal investigating how delegating final decision authority may affect the subsequent capacity for independent reasoning and evaluative judgement.
proposals.scope: The proposed programme examines the relationship between delegated decisions and later independent checking, reasoning and evaluation. It connects human–AI interaction with a broader question about the conditions under which people retain responsibility for judgement.
proposals.relationship: Submission to the ERC-2027-STG call was recorded on 10 October 2026. The submitted proposal is a prospective research programme, not an awarded ERC grant.
proposals.limits: Submission confirmation does not establish an evaluation outcome, a grant agreement or an awarded project period.

proposals.title: Independent STEM Design in Türkiye & the UAE
proposals.full_title: Examining Generative AI Guidance for Preservice Preschool Teachers’ Independent STEM Instructional Design in Two University Contexts in Türkiye and the United Arab Emirates
proposals.setting: Two university contexts in Türkiye and the United Arab Emirates
proposals.summary: A submitted international proposal on how GenAI guidance relates to preservice preschool teachers’ independent STEM instructional-design work.
proposals.scope: The proposed study connects AI-supported instructional design with preschool STEM teacher preparation, keeping independent design performance central to the research question. Türkiye and UAE contexts provide the proposed comparative setting.
proposals.relationship: The proposal was developed jointly with Ahmet Sami Konca at United Arab Emirates University. This proposal is separate from the co-authored publication on scientific agency in preschool STEM.
proposals.limits: The submitted proposal is not included in the supported-project register. A funding award, completed intervention or joint-project result is not claimed.

proposals.title: Visiting-Researcher Collaboration Planning
proposals.full_title: Scientific reasoning, feedback and human–AI learning: planned visiting-researcher applications
proposals.setting: Kırşehir Ahi Evran University, Türkiye · proposed hosting setting
proposals.summary: Preparation of visiting-researcher applications and research agendas around scientific judgement, argument revision, simulation-based feedback and the use of feedback in learning.
proposals.scope: Planning focuses on joint research design and scholarly exchange in scientific reasoning and human–AI learning. Invitation discussions are being used to refine feasible contributions and visit arrangements before an application is finalised.
proposals.relationship: This is a prospective Türkiye-hosted visiting-researcher activity under 2221. It is distinct from the submitted 2219 application for a research visit to Surrey. Discussed invitations are not confirmed visits or appointments.
proposals.limits: No submitted 2221 application, approved visitor, fixed visit schedule or funding award is announced. Potential invitees are not presented as confirmed project staff.

proposals.title: Scientific-Reasoning Task Validity after AI Feedback
proposals.full_title: Developing valid tasks to investigate scientific judgement and the use of evidence-source information following AI feedback
proposals.programme: TÜBİTAK–DFG research concept · possible bilateral or national applications
proposals.lead: Hüseyin Ateş and Moritz Krell · prospective research collaboration
proposals.period: Funding strategy and study duration to be determined
proposals.setting: Türkiye–Germany · Kırşehir Ahi Evran University and IPN Leibniz Institute
proposals.summary: A joint research concept exploring how scientific-reasoning tasks can assess whether learners use evidence provenance to evaluate claims after AI feedback.
proposals.scope: Initial work involves text and graph versions of prototype tasks, explicit rationale and provisional scoring, and discussion of the distinction between identifying sources and using source relationships in scientific evaluation. Task validation and participant testing would be required before strong measurement claims.
proposals.relationship: Moritz Krell reviewed the preliminary concept, suggested developing concrete example tasks and discussed possible bilateral TÜBİTAK–DFG and separate national proposal routes. A revised concept and sample tasks were shared in November 2026. The funding and role arrangements remain open.
proposals.limits: No TÜBİTAK or DFG submission, approved project, confirmed grant, sample-size commitment or validated instrument is claimed.

proposals.title: Physical Robot vs. Virtual Agent
proposals.full_title: Comparing a Physical Humanoid Social Robot and a Screen-Based Virtual Agent in AI-Supported Self-Regulated Environmental Learning: A Mixed-Methods Study with an Active Control Condition among Middle School Students
proposals.period: Proposed research; no awarded project period
proposals.summary: A research proposal comparing a physical humanoid social robot and a screen-based virtual agent in AI-supported self-regulated environmental learning.
proposals.scope: The proposal describes a mixed-methods comparison with an active control condition among middle school students. The research question concerns the educational role of physical and screen-based agents, rather than a reported intervention result.
proposals.relationship: This record belongs in the research-proposal pipeline. It is not an accepted or funded TÜBİTAK 3501 project and is excluded from the supported-project register and funded-research section of the public CV.
proposals.limits: No funding award, approved grant period, current review stage or confirmed resubmission is claimed. No project staffing or study outcomes are inferred from the proposal title.
